CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(id = 1),
  schema_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  graph_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  graph_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  custody TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(custody IN ('owned','observed','')),
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_synced TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  transition_cap TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  layer_order TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(layer_order))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS intent(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  abstraction_level TEXT NOT NULL,
  domain TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  layer TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  source_refs TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(source_refs)),
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  aspect TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('planned','implemented','needs_change','deferred')),
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  tags TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(tags)),
  visibility TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK(visibility IN ('user_visible','internal','')),
  boundary TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK(boundary IN ('inbound','outbound',''))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS codefile(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  language TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_modified TEXT NOT NULL,
  imports TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(imports)),
  symbols TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(symbols)),
  symbol_facts TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(symbol_facts)),
  content_hash TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS quality_rule(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  detection_logic TEXT NOT NULL,
  severity TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(severity IN ('info','warning','error','')),
  inspection_effort TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK(inspection_effort IN ('low','mid','high',''))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS validation(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  validation_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  command TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_run TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_result TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(last_result IN ('passed','failed','not_run','blocked',''))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS note(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  text TEXT NOT NULL,
  author TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  audience TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ignore_rule(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  pattern TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  reason TEXT NOT NULL,
  author TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS delegation(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  pattern TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  target TEXT NOT NULL,
  author TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hypothesis(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  claim TEXT NOT NULL,
  proposal TEXT NOT NULL,
  predicted_outcome TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  author TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_inspected TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  inspected_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vocab_term(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  author TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS persona(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  author TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS relates_to(
  from_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  to_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  inspection_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(inspection_status IN ('uninspected','passing','failing','independent','needs_reverification')),
  criterion TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  confidence REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_inspected TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  inspected_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  priority_score REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY(from_id, to_id),
  CHECK(from_id <> to_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hierarchy(
  parent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  child_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY(parent_id, child_id),
  CHECK(parent_id <> child_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS implements(
  intent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  codefile_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES codefile(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  inspection_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(inspection_status IN ('uninspected','passing','failing','independent','needs_reverification')),
  criterion TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  confidence REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_inspected TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  inspected_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  locator TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY(intent_id, codefile_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS governs(
  rule_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES quality_rule(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  intent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  inspection_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(inspection_status IN ('uninspected','passing','failing','independent','needs_reverification')),
  criterion TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  confidence REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_inspected TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  inspected_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY(rule_id, intent_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS validates(
  validation_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES validation(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  intent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  inspection_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(inspection_status IN ('uninspected','passing','failing','needs_reverification')),
  notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY(validation_id, intent_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS targets(
  hypothesis_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES hypothesis(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  intent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  inspection_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(inspection_status IN ('uninspected','passing','failing','independent','needs_reverification')),
  criterion TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  confidence REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_inspected TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  inspected_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY(hypothesis_id, intent_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS serves(
  persona_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES persona(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  intent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES intent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  inspection_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(inspection_status IN ('uninspected','passing','failing','independent','needs_reverification')),
  criterion TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  confidence REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_inspected TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  inspected_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY(persona_id, intent_id)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journeys(
  persona_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES persona(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

✓ No open findings: no twins, no overlapping ownership, no scatter, no
tangles, no source-fact risks, every rule considered against every
coded intent. The audit gate is green.
✓ No OPEN findings — the audit gate is green.

Hypothesis.author: llm:quality
Hypothesis.claim: smells still rebuild import-derived coupling evidence from raw codefile state on each run, so large-graph smell generation repeats adjacency work that changes only after sync.
Hypothesis.evidence: Read src/db/queries/smells.rs and sync.rs after the current perf work. Coupling-related smells still derive import adjacency from current codefile/import state on each run rather than from a durable sync-produced index, so the claimed repeated work remains real in the code today.
Hypothesis.name: incremental coupling index
Hypothesis.predicted_outcome: smells and related coupling checks reuse sync-produced adjacency data and large-graph smell latency improves without weakening findings.
Hypothesis.proposal: maintain a sync-refreshed coupling index or cached adjacency projection that derived problem signals can read directly instead of recomputing import relationships per command.

Hypothesis.author: llm:quality
Hypothesis.claim: sync still fans out per changed intent/file for RELATES_TO, GOVERNS, TARGETS, and VALIDATES lookups, so large multi-file edits repeat equivalent edge scans and invalidation work.
Hypothesis.evidence: Read src/commands/sync.rs plus relates_to/governs/targets/validates helpers after the bulk-index improvements already shipped. Sync now preloads some ownership and validation state, but ripple writes still fan out through per-intent helpers for multiple edge classes on multi-file edits. The claim is real and bounded to the current code.
Hypothesis.name: bulk-index sync ripple pass
Hypothesis.predicted_outcome: sync touches each relevant ripple edge or validation at most once per run and large multi-file syncs avoid per-intent query fan-out.
Hypothesis.proposal: precompute sync-time indexes for ripple edges and validations, then flag from the bulk maps with deterministic cause ordering.

Hypothesis.author: llm
Hypothesis.claim: When several default direct loom commands read the same graph concurrently, most can fail at GrafeoDb::open with a raw database lock error even though the existing opt-in daemon handles the same JSON workload successfully.
Hypothesis.evidence: Reproduced on this graph: seven parallel direct read commands (status, next --all, smells, coverage, doctor, report, hotspots with --json) returned six rc=1 failures matching 'database file is locked'/'locked by another process'; only coverage completed. After warming the existing opt-in daemon, the same seven commands with LOOM_DAEMON=1 all returned rc=0 and rg found daemon_lock_errors=0. Code review: src/main.rs only tries the daemon when LOOM_DAEMON=1 and --json; src/db/mod.rs wraps GrafeoDB::with_config errors with the raw cause; docs/daemon-design.md documents cross-process locks and daemon MVCC. Tests passed: cargo test daemon_ipc_parity_fallback_skew_and_drain; cargo test daemon_contract_concurrent_sessions_persistent.
Hypothesis.name: teach concurrent direct lock failures
Hypothesis.predicted_outcome: A direct parallel read-command smoke still may fail under cross-process locking, but every lock failure names the recovery path and no raw Grafeo-X001/internal lock text is the primary user-facing guidance; the daemon-backed parallel smoke remains zero-lock-error.
Hypothesis.proposal: Detect Grafeo lock-open failures in the direct DB acquisition path and render a loom-specific recovery message: concurrent direct access is unsupported; serialize commands, use loom batch for grouped writes, or run JSON automation with LOOM_DAEMON=1 so servable commands share the daemon handle. Preserve the daemon as opt-in rather than silently making it the default.

Hypothesis.author: llm:quality
Hypothesis.claim: read-heavy commands still compose many overlapping query helpers over the live graph, so cross-command optimization remains piecemeal and the same logical graph slices are reloaded in slightly different shapes.
Hypothesis.evidence: Read stats.rs, scoring.rs, integrity.rs, and command handlers after the latest optimizations. The code is materially better, but read-heavy commands still layer many overlapping query helpers over the live graph, so a unified snapshot/query layer remains a real architectural performance opportunity.
Hypothesis.name: unified graph query snapshot layer
Hypothesis.predicted_outcome: read-heavy commands share one bulk graph projection per invocation family, making further performance work simpler and reducing repeated table scans across command handlers.
Hypothesis.proposal: add a unified read-only graph snapshot/query layer that bulk-loads shared node and edge slices once and serves status, next, report, doctor, and smells from the same in-memory projection.

Hypothesis.author: llm:quality
Hypothesis.claim: optional discovery still rebuilds token sets, file ownership, and import adjacency for pair scoring on each command, leaving unexplored pair ranking as the main large-graph cost.
Hypothesis.evidence: Read src/db/queries/scoring.rs and smells.rs after the current perf work. unexplored_pairs_scored still rebuilds token/file/import evidence per command and remains the largest optional discovery cost on large graphs; the 2000-intent benchmark confirms discovery-adjacent work is now the main remaining heavy path.
Hypothesis.name: snapshot discovery ranking inputs
Hypothesis.predicted_outcome: discovery commands rank unexplored pairs from precomputed inputs and large-graph discovery latency drops materially without changing ranking semantics.
Hypothesis.proposal: derive a reusable discovery ranking snapshot or sync-maintained adjacency index for unexplored_pairs_scored and related smell ranking.

Hypothesis.author: llm:quality
Hypothesis.claim: status/next/report still rebuild overlapping active-intent, hierarchy, relates, governs, and validation views inside graph_state-oriented helpers, so one command repeats equivalent bulk reads.
Hypothesis.evidence: Read src/db/queries/stats.rs and scoring.rs after the latest perf pass: graph_state still materializes overlapping active-intent, hierarchy, RELATES_TO, GOVERNS, and validation views across graph_state, validate_selection, and normative_coverage. The 2000-intent benchmark is now good but still orientation-heavy, so a shared read-only snapshot remains a real remaining refactor target.
Hypothesis.name: thread graph-state snapshots
Hypothesis.predicted_outcome: status/next/report load each bulk graph slice once per command and the 2000-intent orientation benchmark improves without changing output semantics.
Hypothesis.proposal: introduce a read-only graph snapshot for graph_state, validate_selection, and normative_coverage so orientation commands share one bulk load per command.

Hypothesis.author: llm:quality
Hypothesis.claim: Current storage is Grafeo-shaped rather than backend-neutral: src/db/mod.rs exposes grafeo::QueryResult and grafeo::Value through LoomDb, db_path hard-codes .loom/graph.grafeo, command and daemon paths accept GrafeoDb, query modules contain many GQL execute sites, and docs/tests encode Grafeo lock/query workarounds.
Hypothesis.evidence: Inspected src/db/mod.rs: LoomDb returns grafeo::QueryResult and execute_with_params takes grafeo::Value; db_path returns .loom/graph.grafeo; GrafeoDb/session/Arc are exposed to commands and daemon. rg counts on the current worktree: 181 GrafeoDb refs, 31 grafeo:: refs, 254 execute/execute_with_params sites, and 244 MATCH/MERGE strings across src/tests. src/db/schema.rs states Grafeo is schema-optional and Loom/doctor must enforce vocabulary. src/db/queries/find.rs records Grafeo text search cannot join internal node ids back to properties, so search scans in Rust. docs/daemon-design.md records Grafeo DB-open floor and cross-process lock collisions as daemon motivation. tests/grafeo_probe.rs exists to pin backend quirks. A throwaway SQLite spike at /tmp/loom-sqlite-spike.vSWsNR imported the current export into typed tables in about 0.10s, passed FK/unique constraint checks, FTS search, endpoint updates, rollback, and WAL reader-during-writer behavior.
Hypothesis.name: sqlite-backed graph persistence
Hypothesis.predicted_outcome: A local SQLite loom binary imports the current export, matches the global Grafeo-backed binary on structured read and mutation parity over scratch graphs, enforces FK/unique/status constraints in storage tests, and removes Grafeo-specific query/lock workarounds from command/query code.
Hypothesis.proposal: Replace live graph persistence with typed SQLite-backed graph storage behind a backend-neutral repository/query API, while keeping deterministic loom.graph.json as the migration bridge and global-control artifact.

Intent.description: loom extracts Dart imports and declarations and recognizes Flutter conventions such as pubspec.yaml, lib, test, integration_test, and generated Dart files so Flutter apps get useful static-analysis signals
Intent.name: Dart and Flutter static analysis support

Intent.description: clap-derive CLI surface, dispatch to handlers, bare-invocation orientation
Intent.name: command definitions and dispatch

Intent.description: single-source graph vocabulary declarations (labels, edges, properties, owners, version), shared type structs, graph root targeting helpers, and the GraphReadRepository/GraphReadHandle boundary backed by SQLite
Intent.name: schema vocabulary and repository boundary

Intent.description: loom validate (runs proofs with the session released) and loom init (idempotent bootstrap)
Intent.name: proof and bootstrap handlers

Intent.description: Users can dogfood target/debug/loom against the live SQLite graph, keep committed loom.graph.json as rollback/export state, and promote the local binary only after tests, local graph routing, and export checks pass.
Intent.name: migration cutover and rollback path

Intent.description: subjective aesthetic residue surfaces as manual_check validations with inspected_by set to human, batched into a user-gated lane in loom session prioritised by user presence like align, rulings and blocked
Intent.name: visual-confirm user-gated queue

Intent.description: The migration seeds and applies a small bounded vocabulary for storage, query, export, daemon, schema, parity, and migration work so duplicated responsibility and ownership drift are detectable while the backend is being rewritten.
Intent.name: storage responsibility vocabulary coverage

Intent.description: Servable JSON graph commands use the per-graph daemon automatically by default, with an explicit LOOM_DAEMON=0/false/off opt-out; human-mode, no-graph, and graph-releasing commands keep direct behavior.
Intent.name: automatic JSON daemon path

Intent.description: Command handlers and query consumers depend on typed SQLite graph storage/repository operations and pure snapshot analysis, not backend-specific query strings or legacy storage types.
Intent.name: backend-neutral storage boundary

Intent.description: Schema v4 adds a Hypothesis node (claim, proposal, predicted_outcome, status: proposed/supported/refuted/adopted/rejected, provenance) and a TARGETS edge (Hypothesis to Intent) carrying the standard inspectable meta. Both persist through the deterministic export/import round-trip with two-phase validation, and loom doctor audits their required properties and value vocabularies.
Intent.name: hypothesis node and TARGETS edge

Intent.description: SQLite is the active embedded graph store: every command opens .loom/graph.sqlite directly with foreign keys, busy timeout, WAL/NORMAL pragmas, and transaction boundaries; loom serve is a retired stub rather than a correctness or performance layer.
Intent.name: SQLite direct concurrency policy

Intent.description: The installed Grafeo-backed loom remains the planning/control binary while target/debug/loom is compared on isolated scratch graphs for structured JSON reads, deterministic mutation sequences, and export diffs before any live cutover. Once the SQLite live path is enabled, the same harness is run against that local backend.
Intent.name: global local command parity harness

Intent.description: Builds and maintains a falsifiable intent graph of a codebase (semantic/physical/normative planes) that any LLM drives via structured CLI commands; the graph is durable memory, the context window is the working set
Intent.name: loom: living intent graph CLI

Intent.description: loom extracts Go imports, packages, top-level declarations, test files, and module paths so Go repositories get coverage, coupling, symbol-accountability, sync-narrowing, clone, and smell signals
Intent.name: Go static analysis support

Intent.description: for a user_visible screen, loom guidance generates an HTML mockup as the reaction surface and converts each human reaction into graph deltas, looping until reactions stop changing structure
Intent.name: reaction-driven mockup loop

Intent.description: Adopting a hypothesis writes its predicted_outcome as a not_run Validation attached to the spawned intents; when the validator lane passes it, the hypothesis derives confirmed. Every adopted improvement gets checked for whether it actually delivered.
Intent.name: adoption spawns outcome proof

Intent.description: The SQLite store models Loom's graph as typed node and edge tables with foreign keys, unique endpoint constraints, status CHECKs, queue indexes, JSON-list columns for list facts, and FTS indexes where search uses them.
Intent.name: typed SQLite graph schema

Intent.description: the layering check flags an up-the-order dependency that is clean at every single hop but forms an illegal direction across multiple hops, going beyond the direct-import check
Intent.name: transitive layering-violation detection

Intent.description: sync invalidates IMPLEMENTS, RELATES_TO, GOVERNS, TARGETS, and VALIDATES from indexed SQLite state with deterministic cause notes and without per-edge query fan-out.
Intent.name: sync ripple indexed update path

Intent.description: TARGETS edges on supported hypotheses flip to needs_reverification when a target intent's grounded code changes, with a transition note naming the file. Support earned against old code must be re-earned, exactly like RELATES_TO and GOVERNS claims.
Intent.name: stale hypothesis evidence ripples on sync

Intent.description: loom intent retire marks superseded design deprecated with reason and successor recorded as notes; retired intents are INVISIBLE TO COMPUTATION (queues, coverage axes, centrality, the grid, completeness, sync ripple) and VISIBLE TO HISTORY (node, edges, notes remain); the command reports triggered fallout: orphaned children, files losing their only owner, dangling proofs; independent edges add nothing to centrality
Intent.name: intent retirement contract

Intent.description: loom extracts Swift imports, declarations, test conventions, and Swift package or Apple app layout signals so iOS, macOS, and Swift package repositories receive language-aware static-analysis coverage
Intent.name: Swift static analysis support

Intent.description: loom next --mode align serves active intents ranked by (1+churn-since-confirm) x ln(1+degree) + age/90 where churn counts sync-flip transition notes on the intent's edges newer than its last confirm stamp; the item presents the meaning for a user interview with exactly four outcome commands (confirm/update/retire/add); validator lane, effort mid, dispatch names the align queue
Intent.name: align queue ranks user-intent drift suspicion

Intent.description: loom next --mode quality --take N returns compact GOVERNS work items in one call, grouped by intent so one code-neighborhood read pays for every rule held against it, with prefilled rule_verdict batch-template lines (existing criterion kept, placeholder evidence forced through the gates) and per-item effort from the rule's annotation; capped at 50; symmetric with loom batch's rule_verdict write
Intent.name: bulk quality read grouped by intent

Intent.description: No query-layer read path swallows a parse or extraction failure via unwrap_or_default: malformed stored JSON (imports, source_refs) and missing columns surface as contextual errors, completing the hardening sweep started in codefile/intent/portability/sync
Intent.name: no silent fallbacks in the query layer

Intent.description: validate and saga run continue to execute external commands or HTTP with no live graph handle held, then reopen and record results atomically under the new storage backend.
Intent.name: validation and saga storage isolation

Intent.description: handlers that mutate the graph: intent/edge/codefile/validation/note/rule/ignore plus export-import restoration; all lane-gated
Intent.name: graph-write command handlers

Intent.description: Notes carry an optional audience lane (--for builder|analyzer|fixer|validator|quality); loom note list --for is the lane inbox; loom next sorts notes addressed to the work item's owner role first; quality rules carry inspection_effort (low|mid|high) annotated in the packs and inherited by quality work items
Intent.name: directed handoff notes

Intent.description: the contract stage writes a not_run manual_check Validation VALIDATES-linked to the want intent so the want is falsifiable by default, mirroring the hypothesis-adoption predicted-outcome stub
Intent.name: auto-stub the acceptance validation at the contract stage

Intent.description: clap-derive command definitions and dispatch to command handlers; bare invocation prints orientation
Intent.name: CLI surface and dispatch

Intent.description: vertical spine (tree shape + leaf realization + file reach), coverage reconciliation against disk, doctor audit of schema conformance and provenance lanes
Intent.name: completeness and integrity checking

Intent.description: loom extracts Kotlin package imports, declarations, test conventions, and Android or JVM layout signals so Kotlin repositories receive language-aware coverage, coupling, and smell analysis
Intent.name: Kotlin static analysis support

Intent.description: every command renders human-readable text or --json including a graph_state pulse
Intent.name: dual-mode output

Intent.description: The run-loom benchmark scripts generate a synthetic graph and fail when status, next, smells, or next --all exceed the hot-command budget.
Intent.name: scale benchmark harness

Intent.description: A read-only graph projection bulk-loads shared node and edge slices once and serves status, next, report, doctor, and smells through a common query surface.
Intent.name: shared graph query snapshot layer

Intent.description: Replace Loom's legacy live graph persistence with typed SQLite storage while preserving graph semantics, deterministic export/import, validation/saga honesty, direct CLI operation, and auditability through Loom itself.
Intent.name: SQLite-backed graph persistence migration

Intent.description: On a synthetic graph of >=500 intents and >=1000 edges, loom status / next / smells / next --all each complete in under 2 seconds; the O(N^2) paths (discovery pair enumeration, twin/overlap smells) are bounded or restructured; proven by a benchmark validation against the synthetic graph
Intent.name: scale: hot commands bounded on large graphs

Intent.description: loom guide --mode seed elicits in four ordered stages — want (a user_visible intent plus persona), contract (a validation), logic (internal child intents), physical (implements to code) — one stage and one question at a time
Intent.name: staged want-to-physical seed ladder

Intent.description: Derived audit signals computed over arbitrary-depth traversals of the intent and import graph (RELATES_TO cycles, transitive layering violations, intent islands, bridge centrality), surfaced via smells and graph_state without putting heavy traversal on the per-turn hot path
Intent.name: multi-hop audit layer

Intent.description: The seed ladder specialised for the visual register: reaction-driven with an HTML mockup as the reaction surface and contract, mockup-as-CodeFile that never satisfies production IMPLEMENTS, and machine-first verification with a human visual-confirm queue
Intent.name: UI/UX visual-register seed flow

Intent.description: loom intent update rewrites an intent's name/description in place (same node, same history); a description change ripples one hop like sync but for meaning: passing/independent RELATES_TO and GOVERNS, passing IMPLEMENTS and TARGETS go needs_reverification and linked proofs go not_run (blocked keeps its reason); the old wording is preserved in a decision note; a name-only change ripples nothing; deprecated intents are rejected
Intent.name: intent meaning evolves in place with semantic ripple

Intent.description: Adopting a supported hypothesis links the planned intents spawned from it (or the targets marked needs_change) and records lineage in a decision note. The hypothesis itself never enters build queues, coverage axes, or completeness - conversion hands all real work to the existing intent machinery.
Intent.name: hypothesis adoption converts, never duplicates

Intent.description: unexplored RELATES_TO pairs should be ranked beyond raw centrality (e.g. shared files, shared domain, co-change) so a driver is not pointed at 31 equally-scored pairs on a 10-intent graph
Intent.name: discovery queue ranks pairs by plausibility

Intent.description: loom hypothesis add/list/show/prove/adopt/reject drives the state machine with gates: claim and predicted_outcome must be substantive and falsifiable, the prover's provenance must differ from the proposer's, only a proposed hypothesis can be proven, and only a supported one adopted. Every transition is recorded as an append-only note.
Intent.name: hypothesis lifecycle commands

Intent.description: loom smells: twins, overlapping ownership, scatter, tangles, undeclared coupling, recurrence, normative gaps — computed from graph structure, each with a remedy
Intent.name: derived problem signals

Intent.description: loom guide --mode seed stages a want-to-contract-to-logic-to-physical ladder so a driver populates the intent register implicitly through question order, with visibility captured at seed time, rather than via a new Intent subtype
Intent.name: intent-spectrum seed-flow guidance

Intent.description: loom import --as-planned adopts a source graph's intents, hierarchy, criteria, and validations-as-specs into a fresh target-repo graph, drops all groundings (IMPLEMENTS), marks every leaf planned, and loom guide gains a port mode teaching the re-realization loop; the semantic plane travels, the physical plane is rebuilt in the new language
Intent.name: porting mode: import --as-planned

Intent.description: pure Rust analysis helpers over typed QuerySnapshot data plus annotation-oriented note/vocabulary/meta helpers; SQLite owns storage and mutation while this layer derives queues, integrity, stats, search, smells, and coverage signals
Intent.name: snapshot analysis and annotation helpers

Intent.description: loom vocab maintains a small normalized tag registry for intent tags; write-time validation inlines the registry and drift remedies merge near-duplicate keys so discovery and smells get deliberate collisions.
Intent.name: bounded tag vocabulary

Intent.description: loom extends language-aware import, symbol, test, generated-file, and project detection beyond Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python so popular stacks get first-class static analysis while the graph remains language-agnostic
Intent.name: multi-language static analysis coverage

Intent.description: The YAML saga format: every step names the intent it proves; specs are validated at load (method/JSONPath/json-xor-body) and {{ var }}/{{ env.X }} interpolation resolves vars from initial vars and earlier captures, failing hard on unknown names.
Intent.name: saga spec with first-class intent binding

Intent.description: guide/schema/orientation embed the full driving protocol, including lifecycle transitions and status-family separation, so a cold LLM needs no external docs
Intent.name: self-teaching surface

Intent.description: loom guide --mode seed is explicit-only (never auto-detected) and teaches both loops: elicit (altitude calibrated to user fluency, one question per landing, recommended answers, terminate on enumerable gaps not exhaustion) and align (drive loom next --mode align outcomes); an empty graph's compass routes phase=seed pointing at this guide
Intent.name: seed guide teaches the user interview

Intent.description: UI standards such as accessibility, contrast, touch targets and responsive breakpoints are seeded from rule seed web-ui and mobile and GOVERN the screen and component intents rather than being invented per screen
Intent.name: design-system standards via QualityRule packs

Intent.description: loom find: BM25 keyword search over active intent names+descriptions, ranked; hits carry hierarchy chain, IMPLEMENTS groundings with locators, and a stale-edge freshness count; scoring runs in Rust because grafeo's text-index CALL returns internal node ids unjoinable to properties through GQL; a miss points at loom coverage to distinguish unmapped from nonexistent
Intent.name: ask-the-map keyword search

QualityRule.description: Service (CWE-1088): every outbound call carries an explicit timeout and a bounded retry policy with backoff — no infinite waits, no unbounded retry storms.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Find each HTTP/DB/queue client call: is a timeout set (not the library's infinite default)? Is retry bounded with backoff and jitter?
QualityRule.name: service-timeout-retry-explicit

QualityRule.description: Service: every exposed interface has a committed, versioned contract artifact (schema/IDL/OpenAPI) that consumers can ground against — the seam's single shared truth.
QualityRule.detection_logic: For each endpoint/event/queue the service exposes: where is the contract file, is it in the repo, and does the implementation actually match it?
QualityRule.name: service-contract-artifact

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Security (CWE-284/732): expose the minimum — no debug/admin paths reachable in production flows, no overly-permissive file modes or defaults.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Enumerate what the intent exposes (endpoints, files written, flags) and check each against who actually needs it.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-sec-least-surface

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Security (CWE-89/78/79): untrusted data is never concatenated into SQL/shell/HTML/query strings — parameterize, escape at the boundary, or reject.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Trace untrusted inputs to every interpreter sink (exec/system calls, query strings, format/eval, HTML output) and check the escaping/parameterization at each.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-sec-no-injection

QualityRule.description: Service (CWE-306/862): every externally reachable endpoint authenticates and authorizes before side effects — including 'internal' endpoints reachable from outside the trust zone.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Enumerate reachable routes; for each, find the auth check and confirm it runs before any write or privileged read.
QualityRule.name: service-auth-at-boundary

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Security (CWE-798): no credentials, tokens, or keys in source or config committed to the repo; secrets come from the environment or a secret store.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Scan the intent's files for key-like literals, connection strings with passwords, and tokens; check how the code obtains credentials.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-sec-no-hardcoded-secrets

QualityRule.description: Service: handlers for retriable inputs — webhooks, queue messages, payments — are idempotent; replaying the same message yields no duplicate effect.
QualityRule.detection_logic: For each handler: what happens on exact redelivery? Look for inserts without dedup keys, counters without idempotency tokens, side effects before the dedup check.
QualityRule.name: service-idempotent-handlers

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Reliability (CWE-772/404): every acquired resource (file, lock, connection, handle) is released on ALL paths, including error paths.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Look for acquisitions without RAII/defer/finally protection, locks held across I/O or awaits, and early returns that skip cleanup.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-rel-resource-release

QualityRule.description: trust norm: no verdict-bearing edge may default to passing; compliance/proof states start uninspected and are earned by an inspecting agent
QualityRule.name: green-is-earned

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Performance Efficiency (CWE-834/1050): no unbounded loops/recursion over external-sized data; iteration and queries are bounded, paginated, or capped.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Look for loops over unbounded collections nested in loops (N+1 patterns), recursion without a depth guard, and full scans where a limit exists.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-perf-bounded-work

QualityRule.description: Service (sagas): multi-step workflows define compensation or abort for partial failure — no half-completed state without a recovery path an operator or the code can take.
QualityRule.detection_logic: For each workflow spanning >1 service or transaction: enumerate the failure point after each step and name the compensating action. A missing one is the violation.
QualityRule.name: service-compensation-defined

QualityRule.description: Service: contract changes are additive or versioned — removing/renaming fields or changing semantics requires a version consumers can pin; old versions get a deprecation path.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Diff the contract's history (or its change discipline): were fields ever removed/renamed in place? Is there a versioning convention at all?
QualityRule.name: service-compatible-evolution

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Reliability (CWE-20): external input (CLI args, file content, env vars, network data) is validated before use; invalid input yields a typed error, never corruption or a crash.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Trace each external input to its first use: is there a validation/parse step with an error path before the value reaches logic or storage?
QualityRule.name: iso5055-rel-boundary-validation

QualityRule.description: Service: failures are logged/metric'd with enough context (ids, cause, upstream) to diagnose without reproducing.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Pick the main failure paths: what exactly lands in logs/metrics? Catch-and-ignore blocks and bare 500s with no context are violations.
QualityRule.name: service-observable-failures

QualityRule.description: A storage backend migration cannot replace the global/control backend until structured read parity, mutation parity, deterministic export parity, and rollback/cutover smoke checks pass on scratch graphs built from the same loom.graph.json.
QualityRule.name: migration-parity-before-cutover

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Maintainability (CWE-561/1041): no unreachable or unused code; no copy-pasted logic where one definition should exist.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Look for unused functions/exports, commented-out blocks kept 'just in case', and near-identical logic in sibling files.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-main-no-dead-or-duplicate-code

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Maintainability (CWE-1080/1120): each unit (file, function, intent) owns one coherent responsibility; oversized or multi-concern units are split.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Check unit sizes and concern count; cross-check `loom smells` (tangled_file / scattered_intent) for the same intent.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-main-single-responsibility

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Reliability (CWE-252/248/391): every fallible operation's failure path is handled or explicitly propagated — no silently ignored return value, no exception/panic escaping a boundary uncaught.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Inspect the intent's error paths: ignored Results/return codes, unwrap/expect on external input, bare catch-alls, missing error branches at I/O, parse, lock, and network boundaries.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-rel-no-unchecked-failure

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 Performance Efficiency (CWE-1042/1046): no repeated identical I/O, queries, or allocation in hot paths — cache or hoist invariant work out of loops.
QualityRule.detection_logic: Find work inside loops that is invariant across iterations (reads, compiles, allocations) and repeated identical calls that could be batched.
QualityRule.name: iso5055-perf-no-redundant-work

QualityRule.description: Persistence backends must be isolated behind typed storage/repository operations; command handlers and domain workflows must not depend on backend query language, concrete connection/session types, or backend value/result types.
QualityRule.name: storage-backend-boundary

QualityRule.description: ISO 5055 reliability: no GQL may match or filter a relationship by its own property (grafeo 0.5.x returns nondeterministic results); edges are keyed by endpoint nodes or scanned and filtered in Rust
QualityRule.name: endpoint-matched-edges

QualityRule.description: Service: a dependency outage degrades the service (fallback, partial answer, fast error) — it never cascades into hangs or crash loops.
QualityRule.detection_logic: For each hard dependency: trace what happens when it's down. Look for unguarded startup dependencies and synchronous calls on the hot path with no circuit/fallback.
QualityRule.name: service-graceful-degradation

    run([str(bin_path), "init", ".", "--json"], root)
    run([str(bin_path), "delegate", "add", "services/api/**", "--to", "services/api/loom.graph.json", "--json"], root)
    missing = json.loads(run([str(bin_path), "coverage", "--json"], root).stdout)
    assert missing["delegation_targets_missing"] == ["services/api/loom.graph.json"], missing
    run([str(bin_path), "init", ".", "--json"], svc)
    run([str(bin_path), "export", "--json"], svc)
    covered = json.loads(run([str(bin_path), "coverage", "--json"], root).stdout)

    assert covered["delegated"] >= 1, covered
    assert covered["delegation_targets_missing"] == [], covered
